headline: Space under construction is at its lowest level since Q3 2021, and refurbishments now make up about two-thirds of new starts, pointing to a Grade A supply gap from 2027.
summary: JLL reports central London space under construction at its lowest level since Q3 2021. Savills (as cited by K2 Space) forecasts about 8.5m sq ft of 2026 completions across central London, around two-thirds already pre-let, with 4.85m sq ft in the City; West End completions fall to 1.6m sq ft by 2028. Office starts in 2025 were about 4.8m sq ft against a five-year average of about 6.5m sq ft, and roughly two-thirds were refurbishments (London Construction Magazine). CoStar's forecast expects demand to outpace supply from mid-2027.
insights: Starts in 2025: ~4.8m sq ft vs a ~6.5m sq ft five-year average; refurbishments made up ~two-thirds of start volume (London Construction Magazine, Aug 2026).
Google's 860,000 sq ft King's Cross HQ has completed; OpenAI has pre-let all of Jahn Court for late 2026 (Avison Young).
West End completions are forecast to fall to 1.6m sq ft by 2028 (Savills via K2 Space).
CoStar's UK office forecast expects demand to outpace supply from mid-2027.

signals.title: 2027-2029 Grade A supply gap
signals.rationale: Low construction volumes and slowing starts, set against strong Grade A demand, favour schemes able to deliver in 2027-2029, especially refurbishments that are quicker and lower in embodied carbon.

signals.title: City 2026 completion wave
signals.rationale: About 4.85m sq ft completes in the City in 2026; the unlet portion will compete for the same occupiers in the near term.
